mainTopic: רבי ינאי's tree, building balconies over the street, and how to mourn the חורבן without overburdening the public; end of פרק חזקת הבתים.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the story of רבי ינאי. He cut down his own tree that hung over the public street before ordering another man to cut his, following ריש לקיש's rule: 'fix yourself first, then fix others.' The גמרא then returns to the משנה. A person may pull his wall back onto his own land and build a balcony out to his property line. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about building the balcony later, and רבי יעקב gives a second version where they argue about moving the wall back out. Next, רב הונא says a bought courtyard with balconies may be rebuilt the same way if it falls. The גמרא answers a challenge from a ברייתא about decorated houses by saying that something forbidden is different. That leads into how to mourn the חורבן: רבי יהושע teaches the פרושין to mourn in a balanced way, leaving a small reminder in the house, the meal and a woman's beauty treatments, and ashes are placed on a חתן's head. רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע adds that a גזירה is only made if most people can keep it, since it is better for people to be שוגגין than מזידין. The amud closes with the הדרן for פרק חזקת הבתים.

steps.title: רבי ינאי delays the case and cuts his own tree at night
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי tells the man to come back tomorrow, and that night he has his own leaning tree cut down.
steps.simpleTranslation: Go now, and come back tomorrow. That night, he sent someone to cut down his own tree.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a story. רבי ינאי puts off the case until tomorrow, and that night he quietly cuts down his own tree that also leaned into the street.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי did not want to rule against someone else for something he himself was doing. So before ruling, he removed his own tree. The גמרא will soon explain why he acted this way.

phrases.english: Go now, and come tomorrow.
At night, he sent and had it cut down,
that one of his own.
phrases.notes: He means רבי ינאי's own tree, which also hung over the public street.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a story that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ינאי postpones judgment and first removes his own similar tree.

steps.title: רבי ינאי rules the tree must be cut
steps.stepSummary: The next day רבי ינאי orders the tree cut. The man protests that רבי ינאי has one too, and רבי ינאי answers that his own was already cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: The next day the man came before him. רבי ינאי said: Go, cut it down. The man said: But you, master, also have a tree like that! He answered: Go and look. If mine is cut down, cut yours. If mine is not cut down, you do not have to cut yours.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רבי ינאי's ruling. When the man complains that רבי ינאי has the same kind of tree, רבי ינאי shows that he already cut his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man's protest is fair: a judge should not demand from others what he does not do himself. רבי ינאי's overnight action answers it ahead of time, so his ruling stands firmly.

keyTerms.meaning: master, a respectful way to address a rabbi

phrases.english: The next day he came before him;
he said to him: Go, cut it down.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ: הָא מָר נָמֵי אִית לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: He said to him: But the master also has one!
phrases.notes: The man means a tree of רבי ינאי's that also hangs over the street.

phrases.english: He said to him: Go and see;
if mine is cut down, cut yours down;

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא קוּץ דִּידִי – לָא תִּקּוֹץ אַתְּ.
phrases.english: if mine is not cut down, you do not cut.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The tree over the public street must be cut, and the judge had already removed his own.

steps.title: Why did רבי ינאי change his mind?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי ינאי thought at first, when he kept his tree, and what he thought at the end, when he cut it.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first, what did he think? And in the end, what did he think?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the story. If the tree was not allowed, why did רבי ינאי keep it until now? And if it was allowed, why did he cut it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something seems inconsistent in רבי ינאי's behavior. The גמרא wants to know what changed between "before" and "after."

phrases.english: At first, what did he hold,
and in the end, what did he hold?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעִיקָּרָא מַאי סְבַר וּלְבַסּוֹף מַאי סְבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the story just told.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What explains רבי ינאי keeping his tree at first and cutting it later?

steps.title: At first he thought the public liked the shade
steps.stepSummary: At first רבי ינאי thought the public was happy with his tree because they sat in its shade. When he saw people objecting to a similar tree, he cut his down.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first he thought: the people of the public street are happy with it, since they sit in its shade. Once he saw that they were objecting, he sent someone to cut it down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי ינאי's view of what the public wanted changed. Once he saw that people did object to such trees, he cut his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tree over רשות הרבים can be fine if the public is happy with it. When the public objected to the other man's tree, רבי ינאי realized they probably minded his too, so he removed it.

keyTerms.meaning: they are happy with it, it suits them
the public domain, the public street
they object, they hold it back

phrases.aramaic: מֵעִיקָּרָא סְבַר: נִיחָא לְהוּ לִבְנֵי רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים,
phrases.english: At first he held: the people of the public domain are fine with it,
since they sit in its shade.
Once he saw that they were objecting,
phrases.notes: He saw this in the other man's case, where the tree was being challenged.

phrases.english: he sent and had it cut down.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעִיקָּרָא סְבַר נִיחָא לְהוּ לִבְנֵי רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: His assumption that the public was happy with the tree changed once he saw them object.

steps.title: Why make the man wait until tomorrow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רבי ינאי could have ruled right away and promised to cut his own tree afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him say to him: Go cut yours, and then I will cut mine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי ינאי delayed the case. He could have ruled on the spot and cut his own tree afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Delaying justice seems unnecessary if the ruling was already clear. The challenge pushes for a reason why the order mattered.

keyTerms.meaning: but let him say to him

phrases.english: But let him say to him: Go cut yours,
and then I will cut mine!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new difficulty about the timing in the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's choice to postpone the case to the next day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling was clear, so he could have ruled immediately and fixed his own tree afterward.

steps.title: Fix yourself first, then others
steps.stepSummary: The answer is ריש לקיש's teaching from the פסוק "הִתְקוֹשְׁשׁוּ וָקוֹשּׁוּ": first correct yourself, and only then correct others.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of ריש לקיש, who said: "Gather yourselves and gather" means: adorn yourself first, and afterward adorn others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי ינאי followed ריש לקיש's teaching. You must fix yourself before you tell others to fix themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש reads the words of the פסוק as if they come from the root קשט, "to adorn." So a judge must be clean of a fault before he rules against someone else for it. That is why the order mattered and רבי ינאי cut his own tree first.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי ינאי cut his own tree before ruling, because of ריש לקיש's rule: "קשוט עצמך ואחר כך קשוט אחרים". Correct yourself before you correct others.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle of personal integrity guides how judges and teachers act: they should not demand from others what they do not do themselves.

phrases.english: Because of Reish Lakish, who said:
"Gather yourselves and gather" —
phrases.notes: צפניה 2:1. ריש לקיש reads the word like קשט, "adorn."

phrases.english: adorn yourself,
and afterward adorn others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a principle based on a פסוק that requires a set order.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The order did not matter, so he could have ruled first and cut his own tree later.
steps.terutzMaskana: He had to correct himself before correcting others, so the delay was needed.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: draw back the wall and extend
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a person who wants a balcony may pull his wall back into his own property and build it out to his property line.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he wanted, he may pull back into his own property and extend the balcony.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new topic. It quotes a line from the משנה to set up a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said one may not build balconies or projections out over רשות הרבים. This line allows a way around that: move the wall back onto your own land, and the balcony can stick out only as far as your property line.

phrases.english: But if he wanted —
he draws back into his own and extends.
phrases.notes: He moves his wall back onto his own land, then builds the balcony out over the space he freed up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אִם רָצָה כּוֹנֵס לְתוֹךְ שֶׁלּוֹ וּמוֹצִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to the wording of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may pull the wall back into his own property and extend a balcony up to his property line.

steps.title: Pulled back but did not build: may he build later?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if he pulled his wall back but did not build the balcony right then, may he come back and build it later?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if he pulled back but did not extend, may he later go back and extend?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about the משנה's rule. What if the balcony was not built together with moving the wall?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes pulling back and extending as one act. The question is whether the right to extend stays open if some time passes between the two.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was asked among them
that he go back (and do it)

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
If he drew back but did not extend,
what is the law: may he go back and extend?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a case not spelled out in the משנה quoted in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the right to extend stays if the wall was pulled back without building the balcony at that time.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש disagree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says he may still extend later. ריש לקיש says he may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: if he pulled back, he may extend. ריש לקיש says: if he pulled back, he may not extend.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question in opposite ways. רבי יוחנן allows building later, and ריש לקיש does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, pulling the wall back is enough to keep the right to build the balcony later. For ריש לקיש, the right does not stay if he did not build it at the time he pulled back. The גמרא gives no reasons for this version. Instead, the next step brings a different version of the whole argument.

keyTerms.meaning: he pulled back, so he may extend

steps.whatToRemember: In the case of כנס ולא הוציא: רבי יוחנן says he may extend later, and ריש לקיש says he may not.
steps.confusionAlert: The disagreement is not about the משנה's basic rule. Both agree that pulling back and building at the same time is allowed. They argue only about building the balcony later.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
If he drew back, he may extend.
And Reish Lakish says:
If he drew back, he may not extend.
phrases.notes: He means when he did not build the balcony right then, the case asked about just before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two opposite answers to the question of step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: he may extend later. ריש לקיש: he may not extend later.

steps.title: A second version of the argument: moving the walls back
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב explains that everyone agrees the owner may extend the balcony later. The argument is about returning the walls to their old place, and the opinions are reversed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said to רבי ירמיה בר תחליפא: Let me explain it to you. About building the balcony out later, everyone agrees he may do it. They argue about moving the walls back to their old place. And the opinions were said the other way around: רבי יוחנן says he may not move them back, and ריש לקיש says he may.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of the argument from step 9. It changes both what the argument is about and who holds which opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, the argument was whether he may build the balcony out later. רבי יעקב says that is not argued at all: everyone allows it, since he is building on his own land. The real question is whether he may move the wall back out to where it stood before. Here רבי יוחנן says no and ריש לקיש says yes, which is the reverse of the opinions in step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: I will explain it to you
to extend outward (to build the balcony out)
to return the walls to their original place
it was said the other way around

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two versions. In this version רבי יוחנן is the one who forbids and ריש לקיש is the one who permits, and they are arguing about the walls, not the balcony.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov said to him,
to Rabbi Yirmeya bar Tachlifa:
I will explain it to you:

phrases.aramaic: לְהוֹצִיא – כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּמוֹצִיא,
phrases.english: To extend, everyone agrees that he may extend,
where they argue is about returning the walls to their place;
and it was said the other way around:
Rabbi Yochanan says: he may not return them,
and Reish Lakish says: he may return them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב לְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא, אַסְבְּרַהּ לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the argument in step 9, changing both the topic and which אמורא holds which opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone allows extending the balcony later. On returning the walls to their old place, רבי יוחנן forbids and ריש לקיש permits.

steps.title: Why רבי יוחנן forbids moving the walls back
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן relies on רב יהודה: once the public has started using a path, nobody may take it away from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says he may not move the walls back, because of רב יהודה. רב יהודה said: A path that the public has started using may not be ruined.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי יוחנן's reason, using a rule of רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the owner pulled his wall back, people began walking on the strip of land that opened up. רב יהודה's rule says that once the public has taken hold of a path, the owner may not take it away from them. So the owner cannot move his wall back out onto that strip.

keyTerms.meaning: a path or strip of land
the public has taken hold of it (started using it)
it is forbidden to ruin it (to block the public from it)

steps.whyThisMatters: רב יהודה's rule is an important idea in property law: once the public has established its use of land, that use cannot be taken away.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says he may not return them
because of Rav Yehuda,
as Rav Yehuda said:
A path that the public has taken hold of,
phrases.notes: Here this means the strip where his wall used to stand, which people started walking on.

phrases.english: it is forbidden to ruin it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֵינוֹ מַחְזִיר – מִשּׁוּם דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רבי יוחנן's opinion from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the public uses a path, the owner may not take it back, so the wall may not be returned.

steps.title: Why ריש לקיש allows moving the walls back
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says רב יהודה's rule only applies when the public would be left with no room to walk. Here they still have room.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says he may move the walls back. רב יהודה's rule only applies where there is no extra room. Here there is extra room.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains ריש לקיש's opinion. He limits רב יהודה's rule so that it does not apply to this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש does not reject רב יהודה's rule. He says it only applies when taking the path away would leave people with nowhere to walk. Here the public street is still wide enough, so taking back the strip hurts no one, and the owner may return his wall.
steps.whatToRemember: In רבי יעקב's version, both sides agree with רב יהודה's rule. They only argue whether it applies when the public still has enough room without the strip.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish says he may return them,
those words apply where there is no room,
but here there is room.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: מַחְזִיר – הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא רַוְוחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's use of רב יהודה's rule by limiting where the rule applies.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects applying רב יהודה's rule to this case, but not the rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב יהודה's rule is for a case where the public would be left without room, but here the public still has plenty of room.

steps.title: The משנה: buying a courtyard that already has balconies
steps.stepSummary: Someone who buys a courtyard that already has projections and balconies sticking into the street may keep them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone bought a courtyard that has projections and balconies, it keeps its established status.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. It is setting up a statement of רב הונא about this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person may not build out over the public street. But if he bought a courtyard that already had these projections, we assume they were put there with permission, so he may keep them.

keyTerms.meaning: in its established status (it stays as it is)

phrases.english: If he bought a courtyard that has projections and balconies,
it keeps its established status.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the argument about walls to the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bought courtyard with existing projections and balconies keeps its right to them.

steps.title: רב הונא: if it fell, he may rebuild it the same way
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says that if this courtyard's wall fell, the owner may rebuild it with its projections and balconies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: If it fell, he may rebuild it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא adds to the משנה. The owner's right to the balconies is not lost when the building falls down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says the owner may keep what is already standing. רב הונא goes further: the right stays even after the building falls, so he may rebuild the balconies over the street as they were.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
If it fell, he may rebuild it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: נָפְלָה, חוֹזֵר וּבוֹנֶה אוֹתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the משנה's rule to a building that fell down.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The right to the projections remains after a collapse, so he may rebuild them.

steps.title: Challenge from the ברייתא about decorated courtyards
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that a decorated courtyard bought as is may stay, but if it fell it may not be rebuilt the same way. This seems to contradict רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא challenges: Nowadays one may not plaster, tile, or paint. If someone bought a courtyard that was already plastered, tiled, or painted, it keeps its status. But if it fell, he may not rebuild it that way!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב הונא. In that case, an existing right does not carry over to rebuilding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Decorating homes in these ways is forbidden nowadays. An already decorated courtyard may stay as it is, but once it falls the owner may not rebuild it with the decorations. This looks like the exact opposite of רב הונא's rule that a fallen courtyard may be rebuilt as it was.

keyTerms.meaning: they raised an objection (a challenge from a ברייתא)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא agrees that the bought courtyard may stay as it is. The problem is only about rebuilding after it falls.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One may not plaster and one may not tile
and one may not paint, nowadays.
If he bought a courtyard that was plastered, tiled, or painted,
it keeps its established status.
If it fell, he may not rebuild it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's rule from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that a fallen courtyard with projections may be rebuilt as before.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא shows that a right to keep something that would not be allowed today ends when the building falls. So the same should be true of balconies over the street, against רב הונא.

steps.title: A forbidden decoration is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is about something forbidden (איסורא), so it does not contradict רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A case of something forbidden is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from step 15. The ברייתא and רב הונא are talking about two different kinds of cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's case is about rights against the public. Once the owner gained the right to have projections and balconies, he keeps that right even when he rebuilds. The ברייתא is about a decoration that is an איסור in itself, so once it falls he may not make it again.
steps.whyThisMatters: It separates two kinds of rules. A right someone holds against others can survive a rebuild, but an act that is forbidden in itself cannot be done again.

phrases.english: A forbidden matter is different.
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא is about a decoration that is forbidden in itself, unlike רב הונא's case about rights against the public.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (איסור versus rights against the public)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's ban on rebuilding seemed to contradict רב הונא's permission to rebuild
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא forbids rebuilding because the decoration itself is an איסור. רב הונא's case only involves rights against the public, which the owner already holds.

steps.title: No plastering a house with fine plaster
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a person may not plaster his house with סיד, but it is permitted if sand or straw is mixed in. רבי יהודה says sand makes it fancier and still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A person may not plaster his house with plaster. But if he mixed sand or straw into it, it is permitted. רבי יהודה says: if he mixed in sand, that is fine cement, and it is forbidden. If he mixed in straw, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that spells out the איסור of plastering one's house. Two opinions disagree about whether mixing in sand makes it allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plain bright plaster is forbidden. The תנא קמא says that mixing in sand or straw makes it duller, so it is allowed. רבי יהודה disagrees about sand: sand actually turns it into טרכסיד, an even finer material, so only straw makes it permitted.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that mixing in anything always makes it allowed. According to רבי יהודה, sand makes the plaster finer, not duller.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יָסוּד אָדָם אֶת בֵּיתוֹ בְּסִיד.
phrases.english: A person may not plaster his house with plaster.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם עֵירַב בּוֹ חוֹל אוֹ תֶּבֶן – מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: But if he mixed sand or straw into it, it is permitted.
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: עֵירַב בּוֹ חוֹל – הֲרֵי זֶה טְרַכְסִיד, וְאָסוּר;
phrases.english: If he mixed sand into it, this is fine cement, and it is forbidden;
straw is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לֹא יָסוּד אָדָם אֶת בֵּיתוֹ בְּסִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the plastering איסור quoted in the ברייתא of step 15 (and called איסורא in step 16) with a related ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Plastering a house with plain סיד is forbidden. The תנא קמא allows it if sand or straw is mixed in, while רבי יהודה allows it only with straw.

steps.title: After the destruction, many stopped eating meat and drinking wine
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא relates that after the second חורבן, many פרושין stopped eating meat and drinking wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: When the בית המקדש was destroyed the second time, many people in Israel became פרושין, refusing to eat meat or drink wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about mourning for the בית המקדש. It begins by setting up the story about the פרושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to the plastering ברייתא, since both deal with how to show mourning for the חורבן. Here some people took on a far stricter practice than the חכמים required.

keyTerms.meaning: People who held back from pleasures (ascetics)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: When the Temple was destroyed the second time,
ascetics multiplied in Israel

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא לֶאֱכוֹל בָּשָׂר וְשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁתּוֹת יַיִן.
phrases.english: who would not eat meat and would not drink wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the plastering rule to a related story about mourning practices
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the חורבן, many פרושין gave up meat and wine.

steps.title: רבי יהושע asks why they stopped
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע joins the פרושין and asks them why they do not eat meat or drink wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע joined them and said: My children, why do you not eat meat and not drink wine?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע asks the פרושין to explain their reason. This sets up their answer and his reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not attack them right away. He first gets them to state their reason, so that he can test it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua joined them,
he said to them: My children,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה אִי אַתֶּם אוֹכְלִין בָּשָׂר
phrases.english: for what reason do you not eat meat
and do you not drink wine?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה אִי אַתֶּם אוֹכְלִין בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the practice described in step 18
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the פרושין gave up meat and wine

steps.title: Meat and wine were used on the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The פרושין answer that meat was brought as קרבנות and wine was poured on the מזבח, and now that has stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Should we eat meat, which used to be offered on the מזבח, now that this has stopped? Should we drink wine, which used to be poured on the מזבח, now that this has stopped?
steps.whatsHappening: The פרושין explain their reason. Since meat and wine were part of the עבודה on the מזבח, and that עבודה is gone, they feel they cannot enjoy them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their logic is this: anything that was once used in the עבודה should not be enjoyed now that the עבודה has stopped. This general rule is what רבי יהושע will test in the next step.

phrases.english: They said to him: Shall we eat meat,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ מַקְרִיבִין עַל גַּבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ, וְעַכְשָׁיו בָּטֵל?
phrases.english: from which they offer on the altar, and now it has stopped?

phrases.aramaic: נִשְׁתֶּה יַיִן – שֶׁמְּנַסְּכִין עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: Shall we drink wine, which they pour on the altar,
and now it has stopped?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהושע's question from step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They avoid meat and wine because both were used on the מזבח, and that עבודה has stopped.

steps.title: By that logic, no bread, fruit or water
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע shows that their reasoning would also forbid bread, fruit and even water. They have no answer and fall silent.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: If so, we should not eat bread, since the מנחות have stopped! They answered: we can live on fruit. Then we should not eat fruit, since ביכורים have stopped! They answered: we can eat other fruit. Then we should not drink water, since ניסוך המים has stopped! They were silent.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע takes their rule and pushes it step by step until it reaches something no one can live without. When he gets to water, the פרושין cannot answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each time he names a food used in the עבודה, they find a substitute. Water has no substitute, because ניסוך המים also stopped and no one can live without water. This shows that their rule cannot be applied all the way.

keyTerms.meaning: Flour offerings brought on the מזבח
First fruits brought to the בית המקדש
The water poured on the מזבח on סוכות

steps.whatToRemember: The rule "whatever was used on the מזבח should not be enjoyed now" cannot work all the way, because it would forbid even water.

phrases.english: He said to them: If so,

phrases.aramaic: לֶחֶם לֹא נֹאכַל – שֶׁכְּבָר בָּטְלוּ מְנָחוֹת!
phrases.english: we should not eat bread, since the meal-offerings have already stopped!
It is possible to live on fruit.
phrases.notes: This is the פרושין answering: fine, we will skip bread and live on fruit.

phrases.aramaic: פֵּירוֹת לֹא נֹאכַל – שֶׁכְּבָר בָּטְלוּ בִּכּוּרִים!
phrases.english: We should not eat fruit, since the first fruits have already stopped!
It is possible to live on other fruit.

phrases.aramaic: מַיִם לֹא נִשְׁתֶּה – שֶׁכְּבָר בָּטֵל נִיסּוּךְ הַמַּיִם!
phrases.english: We should not drink water, since the water libation has already stopped!
They were silent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: אִם כֵּן, לֶחֶם לֹא נֹאכַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning given in step 20
steps.kashyaTarget: The פרושין's rule that anything once used on the מזבח should not be enjoyed now
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He pushes their rule to its end: bread, fruit, and finally water would all be forbidden. Since no one can live without water, the rule cannot stand as they stated it.

steps.title: Not too little mourning, and not too much
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע tells the פרושין that it is impossible to skip mourning entirely, and also impossible to mourn so heavily that most people can't keep it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: My children, come and I'll tell you. Not mourning at all is impossible, because the decree already happened. Mourning too much is also impossible, because we don't put a rule on the public unless most of the public can keep it, as the פסוק says: 'You are cursed with the curse, and you rob Me, the whole nation.'
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the פרושין are silent, רבי יהושע gives them the correct middle path for mourning the חורבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He gives two limits. The lower limit is that the חורבן happened, so some mourning is required. The upper limit is that a public rule only works if most people can keep it, and the פסוק says 'the whole nation', meaning a rule binds when the nation as a whole accepted it.

keyTerms.meaning: a decree (here, the חורבן that ה׳ decreed; later, a rule made by חכמים)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the general principle that חכמים do not make a rule for the public unless most people can keep it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: בָּנַי, בּוֹאוּ וְאוֹמַר לָכֶם:
phrases.english: He said to them: My children, come and I will tell you:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא לְהִתְאַבֵּל כׇּל עִיקָּר אִי אֶפְשָׁר –
phrases.english: Not to mourn at all is impossible,
for the decree has already been decreed;
phrases.notes: He means the בית המקדש has already been destroyed.

phrases.english: and to mourn too much is impossible,
for we do not impose a decree on the public

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן רוֹב צִבּוּר יְכוֹלִין לַעֲמוֹד בָּהּ –
phrases.english: unless most of the public is able to keep it,
as it is written: "You are cursed with the curse,
phrases.notes: מלאכי 3:9

phrases.english: and you rob Me, the whole nation."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: בָּנַי, בּוֹאוּ וְאוֹמַר לָכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving the פרושין wrong, רבי יהושע now gives positive guidance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Some mourning for the חורבן is required, but not a level that most of the public cannot keep.

steps.title: Plaster the house but leave a small spot
steps.stepSummary: חכמים said a person may plaster his house, but he must leave a small part unplastered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what חכמים said: A person may plaster his house with סיד, but he leaves a small part of it bare.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע gives the first practical example of balanced mourning, which is the house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of banning plastering, which most people couldn't keep, the rule allows it and keeps a small reminder of the חורבן. This is the middle path from Step 22 put into practice.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what the Sages said:
A person may plaster his house with lime plaster,
and he leaves a small amount in it unplastered;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the middle-path principle to a concrete case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Plastering is allowed if a small area is left bare as a reminder of the חורבן.

steps.title: How big is the bare spot?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much must be left unplastered.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא breaks into רבי יהושע's words to ask for the size of the 'small amount'. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'A small amount' is vague, so the גמרא wants a clear measure.

phrases.english: And how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the measure of the rule just stated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The size of the area left unplastered.

steps.title: An אמה by an אמה, facing the door
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the spot is an אמה by an אמה. רב חסדא adds that it should be opposite the entrance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: an אמה by an אמה. רב חסדא said: opposite the doorway.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer: רב יוסף gives the size and רב חסדא gives the location.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting the spot facing the door means anyone who walks in sees it right away, so it actually works as a reminder.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אַמָּה עַל אַמָּה.
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: A cubit by a cubit.
Rav Ḥisda said: Opposite the entrance.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אַמָּה עַל אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how much.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An אמה by an אמה, placed opposite the entrance.

steps.title: Prepare a full meal but leave out a small item
steps.stepSummary: A person may prepare everything for a meal but should leave out one small item.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may prepare everything needed for a meal, but he leaves out a small item.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע gives the second example of balanced mourning, which is the meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like the house, the meal is allowed in full except for one small missing piece that reminds of the חורבן.

phrases.english: A person may prepare all the needs of a meal,
and he leaves out a small item;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second application of the same principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A full meal is allowed if one small item is left out.

steps.title: Which item is left out of the meal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the small item is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which food is meant. This sets up רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'A small item' needs to be defined so people know what to leave out.

phrases.english: What is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of the item in the meal rule.

steps.title: A dish of small fried fish
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the item left out is a dish of small fried fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: a dish of small fried fish.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא names the item, which is a small side dish of fried fish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is a minor extra dish, so leaving it out is easy for everyone, yet it is still noticeable.

keyTerms.meaning: a dish of small fried fish

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: A dish of small fried fish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers which item is left out.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A dish of small fried fish.

steps.title: A woman does all her beauty treatments but one
steps.stepSummary: A woman may do all her beauty treatments but should leave one small thing undone.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman may do all her beauty treatments, but she leaves out a small thing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע gives the third example, which is a woman's beauty treatments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same pattern repeats: the whole activity is allowed except for one small missing piece as a reminder.

phrases.english: A woman may do all her beauty treatments,
and she leaves out a small thing;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third application of the same principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman may beautify herself fully except for one small thing.

steps.title: Which treatment does she skip?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the small thing is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which treatment she leaves undone. This sets up רב's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, the vague 'small thing' needs to be defined.

phrases.english: What is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of the small thing in the woman's rule.

steps.title: The hair at the temple
steps.stepSummary: רב says she leaves the hair at the side of her forehead (the temple) unremoved.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: the hair of the temple.
steps.whatsHappening: רב names the treatment that is skipped, which is removing hair at the temple.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Women used to remove hair at the temple. Leaving it is a small, personal sign of mourning.

keyTerms.meaning: the hair at the temple (side of the forehead)

phrases.english: Rav said: The hair of the temple.
phrases.notes: He means she doesn't remove the hair there, which women normally removed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers which treatment is skipped.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Leaving the hair at the temple unremoved.

steps.title: The source: 'If I forget you, Jerusalem'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'אם אשכחך ירושלים' is the source for keeping these small reminders.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'If I forget you, ירושלים, let my right hand forget. Let my tongue stick to the roof of my mouth, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: A פסוק is brought as the source for all these small reminders of the חורבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק makes remembering ירושלים something a person must never let slip, even in the middle of daily life and joy. The small missing pieces in the house, the meal and her beauty treatments keep that memory alive.

keyTerms.meaning: to the roof of my mouth

steps.whatToRemember: Mourning the חורבן is a middle path. We don't skip it, and we don't make it so heavy that people can't keep it. Instead we leave a small piece missing: a bare אמה in the house facing the door, one dish left off the meal, and the hair at the temple left on. The source is 'אם אשכחך ירושלים'.

phrases.english: As it is stated: "If I forget you, Jerusalem,
phrases.notes: תהלים 137:5–6

phrases.english: let my right hand forget.
Let my tongue cleave to the roof of my mouth, etc."
phrases.notes: The פסוק goes on: 'if I don't raise ירושלים above my greatest joy.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural basis for the three reminder practices.
steps.raayaObject: The practice of leaving small reminders of the חורבן in daily life.

steps.title: What does 'on the head of my joy' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the end of the פסוק, 'על ראש שמחתי', is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'above my highest joy'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the last words of the פסוק it just quoted. This question sets up the next step, where רב יצחק will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says we should raise ירושלים 'על ראש שמחתי', above the top of our joy. The גמרא wants to know what real-life practice these words point to.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'on the head of my joy': above my greatest happiness
What is it? A question word asking for an explanation

phrases.english: What is 'above my highest joy'?
phrases.notes: These are the closing words of the פסוק from the last step, 'אם אשכחך ירושלים' (תהלים 137:6).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the end of the פסוק quoted in step 32 means
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practice the words 'על ראש שמחתי' refer to

steps.title: Ashes on the head of a groom
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק explains that it means burnt ashes put on the head of חתנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק says: this means the burnt ashes placed on the head of grooms.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק answers the question. 'The head of my joy' means ashes put on the חתן's head on his wedding day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the word 'ראש' in two ways at once. A wedding is the 'top' of a person's joy, and the reminder is placed on the חתן's actual head. So even at his happiest moment he remembers ירושלים.

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak said:
This is the burnt ashes on the head of grooms.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק: זֶה אֵפֶר מִקְלֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words refer to ashes placed on a חתן's head at his wedding

steps.title: Where exactly do the ashes go?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי where on the head the ashes are placed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: Where are they placed?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks a practical follow-up: where on the head do the ashes go? This sets up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know the practice, the question is how to do it. 'The head' could mean many places, so רב פפא wants the exact spot.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
Where does one place it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: הֵיכָא מַנַּח לֵהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Practical follow-up on רב יצחק's answer
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact spot on the head where the ashes are placed

steps.title: In the place of the תפילין, with a proof
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the ashes go where the תפילין go, and brings a פסוק as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the place of the תפילין, as it says: 'To appoint for the mourners of Zion, to give them a garland instead of ashes.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers: the ashes go on the spot where the תפילין of the head are worn. He proves it from a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק promises that in the future the mourners of ציון will get 'פאר', glory, 'instead of' their ashes. Since 'פאר' is a name for תפילין, the ashes must sit in the same place the תפילין later replace.

keyTerms.meaning: Glory or garland; a name for תפילין

phrases.english: In the place of the tefillin,
as it says: 'To appoint for the mourners of Zion,'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 61:3

phrases.english: to give them a garland in place of ashes.'
phrases.notes: 'פאר' is a name for תפילין (יחזקאל 24:17). So the ashes sit exactly where the תפילין go.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's question and supports the answer with a פסוק
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ashes go in the place of the head-תפילין, proven from 'פאר תחת אפר'

steps.title: Whoever mourns for ירושלים will see her joy
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with a promise: anyone who mourns over ירושלים will merit to see her joy.
steps.simpleTranslation: And anyone who mourns for ירושלים merits to see her joy, as it says: 'Rejoice with ירושלים…'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with a comforting promise. Whoever mourns for ירושלים now will one day see her happiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After all the small reminders of sadness, the reward is explained. The same פסוק that tells people to rejoice with ירושלים speaks of 'all who mourn for her', so the mourners themselves are the ones who will celebrate.
steps.whatToRemember: The reminders of the חורבן are not only about sadness. Whoever mourns for ירושלים is promised to see her rebuilt joy.

phrases.english: And anyone who mourns for Jerusalem
merits and sees its joy,
as it says: 'Rejoice with Jerusalem, etc.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 66:10. The rest of the פסוק says 'all who mourn for her', which is the actual proof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the ברייתא about reminders of the חורבן with a promise of reward
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone who mourns for ירושלים will merit to see her joy

steps.title: We should have banned meat and wine, but most people could not keep it
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע says that after the חורבן we really should ban meat and wine, but a גזירה is only made if most of the public can keep it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע said: From the day the בית המקדש was destroyed, it would be right to decree on ourselves not to eat meat or drink wine. But we do not make a decree on the public unless most of the public can keep it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא begins. רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע says a ban on meat and wine would make sense after the חורבן, but it was never made, because most people could not live with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He separates what would be fitting from what can actually be done. The sadness of the חורבן could justify a strong ban. But there is a firm rule that the חכמים don't decree something most of the public cannot keep, so the ban stays only an idea.

keyTerms.meaning: Most of the public is able to keep it

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule for any rabbinic decree: the חכמים do not make a גזירה that most of the public cannot keep.
steps.confusionAlert: He is not saying there is a ban on meat and wine. He says it would fit the situation, and then explains why no such ban was made.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן אֱלִישָׁע:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yishmael ben Elisha said:
From the day the Temple was destroyed,
by right we should decree upon ourselves

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא לֶאֱכוֹל בָּשָׂר וְלֹא לִשְׁתּוֹת יַיִן;
phrases.english: not to eat meat and not to drink wine;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֵין גּוֹזְרִין גְּזֵרָה עַל הַצִּבּוּר
phrases.english: but we do not issue a decree upon the public

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן רוֹב צִבּוּר יְכוֹלִין לַעֲמוֹד בָּהּ.
phrases.english: unless most of the public is able to keep it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן אֱלִישָׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא on how far mourning for the חורבן should go
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ban on meat and wine would fit the חורבן, but no גזירה is made unless most of the public can keep it

steps.title: Under Roman decrees, we should stop marrying altogether
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע adds: since the wicked kingdom stops Torah, מצוות and ברית celebrations, it would be 'right' to stop marrying and having children, so the seed of אברהם would end on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from the day the wicked kingdom spread, which makes evil and harsh decrees against us, stops us from Torah and מצוות, and does not let us enter the 'week of the son' (some say: the 'salvation of the son'), it would be right to decree on ourselves not to marry and have children, and the seed of אברהם אבינו would end by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע gives a second, much stronger 'should have' idea, this time about the Roman persecution. The sentence is not finished yet; the next part will explain why this decree is also not made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rome blocked basic מצוות, including the celebration of a ברית מילה (or, some say, a פדיון הבן). By the same logic as the meat-and-wine idea, it would seem better not to have children at all than to have sons who cannot receive these מצוות. The text stops here with a semicolon, setting up the next line, which pulls back from this extreme.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Week of the son': the celebration around a ברית מילה
'Salvation of the son': the celebration of a פדיון הבן

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a final ruling to stop having children. It is a 'by right we should' line, and the next part of the ברייתא explains why we don't do it.

phrases.english: And from the day the wicked kingdom spread,
which decrees evil and harsh decrees upon us,
and stops us from Torah and מצוות,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מַנַּחַת אוֹתָנוּ לִיכָּנֵס לִשְׁבוּעַ הַבֵּן,
phrases.english: and does not let us enter the 'week of the son',
phrases.notes: This means the celebration around a ברית מילה.

phrases.english: and some say: the 'salvation of the son';
phrases.notes: This means the celebration of a פדיון הבן, redeeming a firstborn son.

phrases.english: by right we should decree upon ourselves
not to marry a woman and have children,
and it will turn out that the seed of Abraham our father
comes to an end on its own;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second 'דין הוא' idea from the same תנא, following the same pattern as step 38 but about the Roman decrees
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under the Roman decrees, it would seem right to stop marrying, so the seed of אברהם would end on its own (sentence continues in the next part)

steps.title: Leave the Jewish people alone
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע concludes that we do not ban marriage and children. It is better that people sin unknowingly than knowingly.
steps.simpleTranslation: But leave the Jewish people alone. It is better that they act unknowingly, and not act on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע finishes his statement. He says we should not actually make the harsh גזירה he just described.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 39 he said it would be 'right' to stop marrying and having children. Now he pulls back: people would not keep such a rule. If we announce it, they would break it on purpose and become מזידין. If we stay quiet, at worst they are שוגגין. This is the same idea as step 38: a גזירה is only made if most of the public can keep it.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave them alone; do not push a rule on them
People who do wrong without knowing
People who do wrong on purpose, knowing it is wrong

steps.whatToRemember: We do not make a rule that people will not keep. Leaving them as שוגגין is better than turning them into מזידין.
steps.confusionAlert: No one is actually told to stop marrying. The 'by right we should' decree from step 39 is never made. He explains that announcing it would only turn people who will marry anyway into מזידין instead of שוגגין.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea 'מוטב שיהיו שוגגין ואל יהיו מזידין' is a well-known principle. It guides when we stay silent instead of warning people about a rule they will not listen to anyway.

phrases.english: But leave the Jewish people alone –
phrases.notes: He means: do not make the harsh rule from the step before.

phrases.english: it is better that they be unknowing,
and not be doing it on purpose.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא הנח להם לישראל מוטב שיהיו שוגגין ואל יהיו מזידין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes and softens the 'it would be right' idea from step 39 by applying the principle from step 38.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: No גזירה against marriage and children. Better that people be שוגגין than מזידין.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק חזקת הבתים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא marks the end of the third פרק, חזקת הבתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, חזקת הבתים.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not part of the discussion. It is the closing line that marks the end of the פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is said when finishing a פרק, as a promise to come back and learn it again. It ends the long פרק about owning property through חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; the line said when finishing a perek
Name of the perek; the rules of proving you own houses and land by using them over time

steps.whatToRemember: פרק חזקת הבתים is now finished.

phrases.english: We will return to you, Chezkat HaBatim

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formal closing of the perek after the final statement.
